mainTopic: How the פסוקים about a daughter who inherits land keep the inheritance from moving to another tribe: the challenge about 'her father's tribe', and the ברייתא about inheritance moving through the son versus through the husband.
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about a daughter who inherits land from both parents. The earlier teaching was that she must marry a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe. The גמרא asks why the פסוק did not simply say 'her father and her mother'. It answers that such wording would have allowed the reverse match, so the actual wording shows that the order matters. Then the גמרא opens a related topic: two ברייתות about how land could leave a tribe, either through her son (סבת הבן) or through her husband (סבת הבעל). The first ברייתא is quoted in full. It proves that במדבר 36:7 is about the son, because במדבר 36:9 already covers the husband. The second ברייתא, about the husband, comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why didn't the verse say 'her father and her mother'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier teaching. If the woman must match both parents' tribes, the פסוק should have named both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this verse should have said: 'to one of the family of the tribe of her father and her mother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that a daughter who inherits from both parents must marry a man linked to both tribes. If that is the rule, the פסוק should have mentioned her mother's tribe too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'the tribe of her father'. If the law really cares about her mother's tribe as well, we would expect the תורה to say 'her father and her mother'. The question is about wording: why does the פסוק say less than the law requires?

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge based on what was just said
It should have said: points out the wording we would expect

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if she must marry a man whose father matches her father's tribe and whose mother matches her mother's tribe.

phrases.english: this [verse]: "to one of the family of the tribe
of her father and her mother" — it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַאי ״לְאֶחָד מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת מַטֵּה אָבִיהָ וְאִמָּהּ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier derivation that the woman must match both parents' tribes in a specific order.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a daughter who inherits from both parents must marry a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both tribes matter, the פסוק should have named both parents, not only 'her father'.

steps.title: That wording would have allowed the reverse match
steps.stepSummary: Had the פסוק said 'her father and her mother', we might have allowed any man linked to both tribes, even in reverse order. The actual wording teaches that the order matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were written like that, I would have said that even the opposite is fine. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. 'Her father and her mother' would have been too loose and would have allowed the opposite arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'father and mother' in the פסוק, any man connected to both tribes would seem fine. That includes a man whose mother is from her father's tribe and whose father is from her mother's tribe. The תורה's wording, 'the tribe of her father', shows that his father must match her father's tribe, so the reverse is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought: the mistaken idea we might have had
It teaches us: what the actual wording comes to show

steps.whatToRemember: The order matters. His father must be from her father's tribe, and his mother from her mother's tribe. The reverse is not allowed.

phrases.english: If it were written like this,
I would have said even the opposite [is allowed],
phrases.notes: The 'opposite' is a man whose mother is from her father's tribe and whose father is from her mother's tribe.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that it is not].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתִיב הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא אֲפִילּוּ אִיפְּכָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the suggested wording would have led to a wrong conclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With 'her father and her mother' in the פסוק, any man connected to both tribes, in either order, would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording 'the tribe of her father' requires his father to match her father's tribe, so the reverse is not allowed.

steps.title: Two teachings: inheritance moving through the son and through the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces two ברייתות. One is about land moving through the son, and the other about land moving through the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught regarding transfer through the son, and it is taught regarding transfer through the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up what comes next. The גמרא tells us there are two ברייתות, and it is about to quote them one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who inherits land and marries into another tribe could cause her land to leave her tribe in two ways. Her husband could inherit it from her (סבת הבעל), or her son could inherit it from her (סבת הבן). Each ברייתא ties a different פסוק to one of these two ways.

keyTerms.meaning: The land moving to another tribe through her son
The land moving to another tribe through her husband

steps.confusionAlert: Both ways come from the same woman marrying into another tribe. The difference is only who inherits from her: her son or her husband.

phrases.english: It is taught regarding transfer through the son,
and it is taught regarding transfer through the husband;

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא בְּסִבַּת הַבֵּן, וְתַנְיָא בְּסִבַּת הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about the פסוקים against land moving between tribes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two ברייתות: one about land moving through the son, and one about land moving through the husband.

steps.title: The first ברייתא: this verse is about the son
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא says that 'no inheritance shall transfer from tribe to tribe' speaks about the land passing through the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught regarding transfer through the son: 'So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer from tribe to tribe' — the verse speaks of transfer through the son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first ברייתא. It says that one specific פסוק is about the land moving to another tribe through her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her son's tribe follows his father, so if she married into another tribe, her son belongs to that tribe. When he inherits her land, it leaves her tribe. The ברייתא says this פסוק is about exactly that case.

keyTerms.meaning: No inheritance shall transfer, or turn over

phrases.english: It is taught regarding transfer through the son:
"So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer
from tribe to tribe" —
the verse speaks of transfer through the son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first of the two ברייתות announced in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: במדבר 36:7 speaks about land moving to another tribe through the son.

steps.title: Maybe this verse is about the husband instead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether this פסוק might be about land moving through the husband rather than the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it is about transfer through the son. Or perhaps it is only about transfer through the husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own claim. It suggests the פסוק could just as easily be about the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, the פסוק does not say whether the son or the husband is the one through whom the land moves. So the ברייתא needs a reason for reading it as being about the son. This question sets up the proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You say: introduces a challenge to the proposed reading
Or perhaps it is only: offers another possible reading

phrases.english: You say: regarding transfer through the son;
or is it perhaps only regarding transfer through the husband?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: בְּסִבַּת הַבֵּן; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּסִבַּת הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why read במדבר 36:7 as being about the son rather than the husband?

steps.title: A different verse covers the husband, so this one is about the son
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק already covers land moving through the husband. So the first פסוק must be about the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says, 'So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe,' that already speaks of transfer through the husband. So how do I explain 'So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer from tribe to tribe'? The verse speaks of transfer through the son.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. A later פסוק (36:9) is about the husband, so the earlier one (36:7) must be teaching about the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. 36:9 already covers the husband, so 36:7 must teach something new: the case of the son. Each פסוק gets its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says: brings in another פסוק as proof
This is already stated, so it is already covered
How do I explain, or what purpose do I give to, this פסוק?

steps.whatToRemember: There are two פסוקים with two jobs. 36:9 is about land moving through the husband, and 36:7 is about land moving through the son.

phrases.english: When it says:
"So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe,"
that already speaks of transfer through the husband;
so how do I explain

phrases.english: "So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer from tribe to tribe" —
